unmapped_findings: AN850-T retained austenite (RA) content before deformation was 0.6%, and after tensile fracture the austenite fraction decreased to 0.002 (0.2%) (b0036, figure_012).
During tensile deformation AN850-T transformed retained austenite into deformation-induced martensite (DIM), reaching a final DIM fraction of about 0.28% (figure_007).
AN850-T showed a broadened DIC strain-concentration band during deformation, with no second local strain-concentration annotation unlike AN800-T (figure_009).

At 850 °C, significant migration of carbon and manganese into the B/TM and FM regions resulted in local oversaturation of alloying elements, increasing strength but also brittleness of the hard domains; in AN850-T the hard domains were severed during fracture (b0131).

AN850-T fracture surface showed dimples plus quasi-cleavage regions, mostly originating from fresh martensite; the dimple size distribution was bimodal (average 1.31 µm, Peak I 0.60 µm, Peak II 1.78 µm) (b0131, figure_011).
For AN850-T, the lower retained austenite content resulted in no significant strain-hardening phenomenon induced by DIM (b0128).
The B/TM strength contribution reached 54% of the flow stress at necking strain for AN850-T, the highest among the three tempered samples (b0128).
No dynamic propagation instabilities such as Lüders bands or Portevin-Le Chatelier bands were observed in any of the samples (b0044).
